stories.title: Analytical quality by design based HPLC method development validation and green assessment for tenofovir alafenamide quantification in ultradeformable vesicles
stories.description: QbD makes it easy to develop an analytical method using a logical process to evaluate and control critical characteristics for robustness and ruggedness, providing more reliable methods than traditional trial-and-error approaches. It enables understanding of critical factors affecting product performance. The HPLC method was developed using a QbD approach on the Agilent 1260 Infinity II system equipped with a Shim-pack GIST-C18 (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 μm) for determination of TAF. The analytical target profile and critical performance attributes were set, followed by risk assessment using failure mode and effects analysis and fishbone diagram. Critical method parameters were optimized by experimental design, and validation was done based on ICH Q2 (R2) Guidelines. Flow rate, injection volume, column temperature, and percentage of methanol were identified as critical variables. The optimized parameters (0.7 mL/min, 15 µL, 50 °C, 70% methanol) gave a peak area of 258.85 mAU, tailing factor of 0.936, theoretical plates of 13791.15, retention time of 5.476 min, and desirability of 0.814 indicating satisfactory optimization. The calibration graph was linear in the concentration range of 50ng/ml to 40mcg/ml at 261 nm. Precision, robustness, and recovery studies indicated %RSD of less than 2% and mean recovery of 98–102%.

stories.title: Dual-channel 1D-CNN-BiLSTM transfer learning for diagnosing tooth breakage across circular saw blade wear stages
stories.description: As the core cutting tool for dismantling stainless steel cladding of spent fuel assemblies, the circular saw blade is prone to tooth breakage failure, which can directly lead to reduced machining accuracy, decreased production efficiency, and even equipment safety accidents. Furthermore, dynamic changes in the wear stage of the circular saw blade cause shifts in the distribution characteristics of cutting signals, posing a challenge for domain adaptation in cross-wear stage tooth breakage diagnosis. To address the issues of scarce fault annotation data for each wear stage in actual production and the insufficient generalization ability of traditional models, this paper proposes a transfer learning fault diagnosis method based on a dual-channel 1D-CNN-BiLSTM network. First, the method effectively preprocesses dual-channel vibration signals during circular saw blade cutting, including effective signal extraction and sliding window framing, to construct a source-domain fault dataset for new saw blade tooth breakage and target-domain datasets for each wear stage. Subsequently, a hybrid 1D-CNN-BiLSTM network is designed, where 1D-CNN extracts multi-scale local spatial features of the saw blade cutting signals, and BiLSTM captures bidirectional temporal dependency features. This network is pre-trained in the source domain as a general fault feature extraction model. Finally, a fine-tuning strategy combining layer replacement and adaptive learning rate factors is adopted, freezing the bottom feature extraction layers and retraining the top classification layer, thereby achieving efficient transfer of fault knowledge from the source domain (new saw blade tooth breakage) to the target domain (various wear stages). Using three types of circular saw blade tooth breakage as the research object and comparing with methods such as SVM, 1D-CNN, LSTM, ResNet and DANN, experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 97.9% in cross-wear stage tooth breakage fault diagnosis, significantly outperforming other methods. It effectively solves the transfer diagnosis problem of tooth breakage faults across wear stages and improves the cutting efficiency of stainless steel cladding of spent fuel assemblies.
